name: Ramco Systems Ltd
tagline: Rare Indian owned-IP enterprise-software product company (global Payroll, Aviation/Defence MRO, ERP) that posted its first full-year profit in FY26 on a genuine cost/margin reset (EBITDA margin 14% -> 24%, near debt-free) - but Q1 FY27 consolidated PAT collapsed to ~Rs 0.6 Cr, 5-yr revenue CAGR is ~2%, recurring revenue has barely scaled in a decade, and the stock now trades at ~36x P/E
business_overview: Ramco Systems sells cloud enterprise software products -- global Payroll/HR, Aviation & Defence MRO, and ERP (strength in textiles, cement, manufacturing, logistics). It is a rare Indian product company with owned IP and a recurring-revenue model, kept alive across a long loss stretch by promoter (Ramco group) support. New MD (ex-logistics) since ~FY25; strategy is an 'AI-native global enterprise software' pivot (Chia AI / RPA) with heavy front-loaded sales, marketing and re-platforming spend.

fundamentals_narrative: FY26 is a real inflection on the cost and balance-sheet side: first full-year profit after a long loss run (consolidated PAT Rs 41.84 Cr), EBITDA margin up to 24% from 14%, D/E ~0.12, employee cost normalised, recurring-revenue share up to 57% (+15% YoY). Recent wins add aviation/defence credibility - Tata Advanced Systems (IAF C-130J MRO), Safran Helicopter Engines (Sep 2026), ST Engineering (AI-led MRO), Korean Air, CFS Aero, UAMCO - and the unexecuted order book is ~USD 152 Mn. But the turn is cost/margin-led, not demand-led: 5-yr revenue CAGR is ~2%, absolute recurring revenue has crept from ~USD 40 Mn to ~USD 48 Mn over many years, and the domestic footprint is tiny against SAP/Oracle/Workday. Q1 FY27 is the immediate problem - consolidated PAT collapsed to Rs 0.56 Cr (standalone Rs 8.69 Cr) on ~flat revenue and front-loaded AI-transition / sales-and-marketing spend in 'other expenses', plus a small one-time tax-regime charge. Bulls call it seasonal-plus-transitional; bears call it the same demand air-pocket that hit them during COVID. Valuation has re-rated to ~36x P/E / ~6.5x P/B, so this is no longer a cheap turnaround. CFO R Ravikula Chandran retires 30-Nov-2026; Gayathri R (CA, with Ramco since 2003) succeeds him - an orderly internal transition.
technical_read: Not pulled. Thread notes promoter holding up ~2% in recent quarters and some new HNI entries; stock had a strong March-quarter-led run then a disappointing Q1.
sentiment_summary: Thread has a decade of history; recent (2024-26) tone is 'credible turnaround, unproven scale'. LarryWink (trusted) is the constructive anchor -- lays out the FY26 turnaround, order book and margin-discipline case but explicitly gives it 'a rope for the next 1-2 quarter results' on three checks (OPM back above 20%, recurring revenue actually rising, services revenue stabilising). Nitya_Shah (largest family position, biased, not trusted) sees a 2-3 year story if global expansion executes. nav_1996 and nagarajj (the latter a ~decade-long tracker) are the skeptics: chequered history, missed SaaS boom, recurring revenue not scaling, lumpy services revenue, slow client decision-making. Snowman (trusted, invested) flagged the Q1 PAT drop and asked if it was expected. No unambiguous high-conviction buy call from a trusted user -- LarryWink is conditional.
community_signal: Trusted users are split and conditional: LarryWink constructive-but-'show me', Snowman invested-but-worried, others (via non-trusted decade-long trackers) skeptical on scale. Net: a genuine-turnaround acknowledgement with real doubt on whether it scales. No conviction floor.

trusted_signals.note: Constructive -- 'fairly credible turnaround': FY26 first profit, ~24% EBITDA margin, ~Rs 1,460 Cr order book, aviation/defence focus; a 12-18% revenue CAGR with margin expansion 'doesn't look unreasonable' IF execution holds

Tempered -- acknowledges skeptics' points (slow recurring growth, lumpy services, infrequent large deals); willing to give '1-2 quarters' and will judge on OPM >20%, recurring revenue actually rising, services stabilising

bse_notes: No corporate-action red flags surfaced. Watch-items: long history of promoter bailouts / capital support; a CEO 'trading plan' disclosure questioned on-thread; heavy discretionary 'other expenses' make quarterly profit hard to model.

verdict_headline: A real FY26 cost/margin turnaround with genuine aviation/defence MRO wins, but Q1 FY27 consolidated PAT collapsed to ~Rs 0.6 Cr, a decade of non-scaling recurring revenue is unresolved, and the stock trades at ~36x P/E - thesis_fit -> neither, conviction Low
verdict_reasoning: FY26 is a genuine reset: first full-year profit (consolidated PAT Rs 41.84 Cr), EBITDA margin 24% (from 14%), near debt-free, recurring share up to 57%. But the most recent quarter went the wrong way - Q1 FY27 consolidated PAT collapsed to Rs 0.56 Cr on ~flat revenue and front-loaded AI/S&M spend.

The small/mid-cap live-inflection carve-out does not rescue the return-magnitude label: that rule needs a STRONG recent quarter, and Q1 FY27 was weak. The structural doubt (recurring revenue stuck near USD 48 Mn for years, 5-yr revenue CAGR ~2%) is unresolved.

four_box score 2.5 (moat yes - certified MRO switching costs + India defence tailwind; tailwind/tam weak - no top-line growth, sub-scale vs SAP/Oracle/Workday; valuation weak - P/E ~36x, P/B ~6.5x). No decision-table exception applies (valuation not yes, growth not un-ignorable, not a large-cap) -> thesis_fit neither.
